title: Wide Ball
intro: Every wide ball puts your groin at full length and asks it to take load. So it's worth training that position under load. We walk first, open the position, then load it. Do it on a light day.

You need something firm at about knee height for the Copenhagen, like a bench or a sturdy sofa seat. A chair only works pushed hard against a wall so it can't slide. Not a bed. An easy bike does the walk's job if you'd rather.

before.label: Who it's for
before.text: A groin that's tight, not one that's strained.

before.label: Stop and get it looked at
before.text: If you've strained your groin in the last couple of months, it grabs when you push off, you have pain at the pubic bone or low in the belly, or you feel a lump or bulge in the groin. Also a sharp pinch at the front of the hip in the deep positions that keeps happening.

before.label: While you train
before.text: Tired or a bit sore is fine. Sharp, in one spot, or worse first thing in the morning means back off and get it looked at.

before.label: Keep clear
before.text: It leaves the adductors sore for about two days. Keep it two days clear of your next match and of speed or braking work on court.

before.label: First time
before.text: Do just one set of each loaded exercise and see how you feel in two days.

exercises.name: Cossack Squat
exercises.note: Go only as deep as you can control and come up a little if the front of the hip pinches.

exercises.name: Copenhagen Plank
exercises.note: Stop the set when your hips start to drop, even if that's before fifteen seconds.
